chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal from Uqbah ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ruled that the fruit of the palm tree belongs to the one who pollinates it, unless the buyer stipulates otherwise.
ai.seo_question: Who owns the fruit of a palm tree if it is sold?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the default ownership of agricultural produce, linking it to the labor of pollination (*tabeer*) rather than mere land ownership. This ruling serves as a foundational principle in Shia jurisprudence for sales contracts (*bay'*), emphasizing that the right to harvest belongs to the pollinator unless explicitly transferred by stipulation. It reflects the practical economic norms of Medina during the Prophet’s time, ensuring fairness in agricultural trade.
